prompt.alinti: NVIDIA just flagged 1 in 20 cloud skills as straight-up malicious. And a skill is just a text file that runs with everything you have access to. So it can read your API keys and walk straight into your client folders. The instructions can be hidden in the text you can't see when you open it. The file looks completely clean to you and you run it anyways. A quarter of the skills out there have a security hole in them. So NVIDIA built a scanner and put it on GitHub for free. It's called Skill Spectre. Just point it at any skill and it hands you a risk score out of 100 and tells you flat out whether it's safe to install. It's checking 70 patterns across 17 categories. So it catches the skill harvesting your environment variables, the one pulling a script off the internet and running it, and the one setting up a cron job after you close the terminal so it keeps running. And if you've already got a full folder of skills that you've never checked, point it at the whole folder and it scans every single one of them at once. Then plug it into Claude as an MCP and Claude runs the scan itself before anything new gets installed. So you stop having to remember before you install skills. The reason to trust this is that NVIDIA runs this on their own skills catalog and nothing gets published there until it passes this exact scan. Just comment 'scan' and I'll send you the full install and Claude setup and share this with someone who wants to install Claude skills safely.
